help.quickStart.body:
# Quick start

1. Open Graphics library at the top right and browse or search for a resource. Add it directly to the canvas, or add it to the graphics list for reuse.
2. In the graphics list, click + Add to create a canvas node.
3. Select a node and edit its colors and parameters in the inspector. Ctrl/Cmd-click to select several nodes; the same tabs edit shared settings. Matching shapes also share shape parameters. Transform / Layout provides alignment and distribution. Edit primary selection to change individual curves.
4. Finish the static design before recording animation. Enable Record, move the playhead and adjust a parameter, then stop recording and play to review.
5. File → Save project preserves editable content. Export creates PNG, SVG, PSD and animation deliveries.

## Resources, instances and previews

The graphics library is the resource source, the graphics list stores reusable copies, and canvas nodes are instances. Editing an instance does not overwrite the library. Preview zoom, solo mode and checkerboards affect viewing only. Set export size, channel and transparency in Export. Spatial seamless repetition, keyframe loops and built-in time-based motion are separate mechanisms; enabling a loop does not guarantee matching endpoints.

## Generate normals from an image

Add an image with Color and alpha mode. Its luminance supplies height: bright is high, dark is low. Set Texture channel to Normal and adjust generation settings. Use 2D to inspect the normal texture or 3D to inspect its lighting on a neutral material. Choose Output channel → Normal separately when exporting.

## Workspace and help

Use Layout for defaults, animation and canvas-focused layouts. Drag tabs to edges to split or to the center to merge. Float with ↗ and resize separators. Reopen closed panels from Layout. Layouts are saved in this browser separately from project content. Search help or choose a topic on the left. Authoring Skill helps external AI create resources; Effects Skill explains editor workflows. Neither connects this editor to an AI service.

## Online analytics

The official GitHub Pages and WorkBuddy versions use Baidu Analytics for basic traffic data. Baidu processes the network, browser and visitor identifiers needed for statistics. Pageview paths exclude shared canvas parameters and sharecode; project names, images and nodes are not intentionally submitted. Automatic click tracking is disabled. Offline, local and other-domain deployments do not load analytics.

modules.blendingHelp: The blend mode controls how this node combines with earlier content in the same group.

ribbon.parametersHelp: Continuous strands run horizontally; twisting gathers them into folds. Strand width is relative to graphic height and keeps the same proportions in preview and export. ribbon.strandsHelp: Independent strands vary in distortion phase, width and opacity. Strand variation controls width and brightness differences. Width is relative to graphic height with automatic subpixel coverage. Horizontal seamless mode rounds frequencies and disables end fading.

fx.help.blur: Softens color, alpha edges and height. Radius uses a 512-pixel short-edge reference.
fx.help.bloom: Extracts highlights above the threshold, blurs and adds their glow.
fx.help.sharpen: Enhances local color and height differences.
fx.help.chromatic: Offsets red and blue horizontally, vertically or radially. Distance uses a 512-pixel short edge.
fx.help.posterize: Controls shadow and highlight levels. Zero highlight levels follows shadows, preserving legacy posterization.
fx.help.pixelate: Samples the composited node in blocks. Size uses a 512-pixel short-edge reference.
fx.help.vignette: Blends selected edges towards a color while retaining alpha and height.
fx.help.scanline: Overlays scanlines within the node region. Zero speed freezes motion; phase offsets the lines.
fx.help.kaleidoscope: Folds the composited node into symmetrical sectors.
fx.help.mirror: Folds the node region into mirrored repeats along selected axes.
fx.help.swirl: Warps the composited node or group, fading with distance from its center.
fx.help.edge: Detects internal luminance edges and overlays their color, preserving alpha.
fx.help.tricolor: Maps result luminance to shadow, midtone and highlight colors without changing height.
fx.help.radialMask: Sets a center, radius and feather in node coordinates, masking alpha and height together.
fx.help.unblack: Converts black-backed brightness into alpha while recovering color and retaining existing transparency.
fx.help.normal: Creates normal colors from current height, preserving alpha and height. Later color filters affect these colors; normal output is computed separately.
fx.help.sketch: Redraw this node with Rough.js. Choose solid, hachure, cross-hatch, zigzag, dots, dashed, zigzag-line or sunburst; preserve original colors or draw outlines only. Style-specific controls appear as needed. A fixed seed reproduces every style.

examples.sketchStyles.name: Hand-drawn style comparison
examples.sketchStyles.description: Nine hearts show the original, solid, hachure, cross-hatch, zigzag, dots, dashed, zigzag-line and sunburst styles, left to right and top to bottom. Select each node to inspect its settings.
examples.lightningStrike.name: Lightning strike
examples.lightningStrike.description: Main bolt and branches, contact flash and residual sparks. A 1.2-second one-shot with appearance, flicker and dissipation. Edit colors per layer and export with transparency.
examples.frostNova.name: Frost nova
examples.frostNova.description: Two expanding icy rings, radial crystals, debris and cold mist. A complete 1.6-second burst; replace debris units or adjust their count in the group arrangement.
examples.fireExplosion.name: Fire explosion
examples.fireExplosion.description: White-hot core, volumetric fire, shock ring, trailing smoke and embers. A 1.8-second one-shot with separate time tracks for fire and smoke.
examples.holographicImpact.name: Holographic shield impact
examples.holographicImpact.description: Circular honeycomb shield, scan lines, an off-center contact highlight and ripple. A 1.4-second appearance, impact and fade, with a separate shield mask.
examples.replaceableDotArray.name: Replaceable-unit dot array
examples.replaceableDotArray.description: Select the outer group and open Transform/layout to edit rows, columns, size, position jitter and size variation. Circles, stars and crosses cycle in order. Replace direct children with images or custom components; disable extra candidates to use one unit.
examples.cleanRings.name: Clean shock rings
examples.cleanRings.description: Flat rings with a soft rim flowing outward in a four-second loop. Select the ring node to edit frequency, base radius, width, speed and phase.
examples.liquidRipples.name: Liquid ripples
examples.liquidRipples.description: Closed sine-wave rings with soft glow. Angular waves sets the ripple count and distortion its amplitude. A four-second loop; switch to flat or noise waves as needed.
examples.energyPulses.name: Energy pulses
examples.energyPulses.description: Noise-disturbed rings and outer glow with independent width and radius. A four-second loop; negative flow speed contracts the energy inward.
examples.coreHalo.name: Core and halo
examples.coreHalo.description: A pale core and blue outer halo with independent size, range, strength and color. A three-second breathing loop on transparency, ready to save as a reusable component.
examples.auroraCurtain.name: Aurora curtain
examples.auroraCurtain.description: Three asynchronous light bands, a refraction membrane, foreground strands and dust. A smooth six-second back-and-forth loop with independent colors and timing, exported transparently.
examples.holyCurtain.name: Holy light curtain
examples.holyCurtain.description: Golden layered bands and a soft core with membrane, strands and dust. A six-second back-and-forth loop; change foreground and background opacity to adjust depth.
examples.energyBarrier.name: Energy barrier
examples.energyBarrier.description: Cool light curtains, a subtle hex grid, refractive edges and particle strands. A six-second closed motion; reuse individual layers as components in other effects.
export.gifLimitations: GIF supports up to 256 colors and binary transparency. Alpha threshold: 0–255. Disable transparent background to preserve soft edges over the background. Export is capped at 50 FPS with 10 ms timing steps. Shared palettes sample up to 12 frames; use per-frame palettes for rich color changes.
export.gifSummary: GIF · {0} × {1} · {2} frames · {3} FPS · {4} s playback · up to {5} colors
export.gifInvalidSize: GIF frame dimensions must be 1–4096 pixels.
animation.cycleExplanation: Time for one 0→1 progress cycle, independent of export duration. Formula animations use continuously elapsed seconds.
export.durationExplanation: Animation cycle controls 0→1 progress speed; export duration controls how long to record, including multiple or partial cycles. Formula seconds keep advancing.
export.atlasPreviewHelp: Choose Generate preview to show the atlas below. Preview frames use up to 128 pixels on the longest side and shrink further when needed. All frames and columns are preserved; delivery dimensions stay unchanged.
export.atlasPreviewResult: Preview atlas {0} × {1}, {2} frames. Preview resolution may be reduced.
export.previewHelp: Preview the current export settings without switching formats. Preview frames use up to 128 pixels on the longest side and shrink further when needed. Sequences/atlases display in 8-bit; GIF uses its current encoding settings. Delivery dimensions and precision stay unchanged.
export.previewStale: Settings changed. The previous result is shown; update the preview.
fx.help.halftone: Creates round, square or line halftones from luminance, or rotated RGB screens. Preserves alpha and height; paper color stays inside existing content.
fx.help.dither: Quantizes RGB, grayscale, two-color or four-tone handheld palettes with Bayer or seeded-noise dithering. Preserves alpha and height. Cell size uses a 512px short edge.
fx.help.glitch: Displaces random slices and separates RGB channels, moving alpha and height with the image. Zero rate freezes motion. Seed and phase reproduce frames without playback history.
fx.help.zoomBlur: Accumulates samples outward, inward or both ways to form streaks. Processes color, alpha and height together. Full effect inside the inner radius fades to zero at the outer radius. Distance uses a 512px short edge.
fx.help.kuwahara: Smooths low-variance color regions for a painted look. Choose four quadrants or eight elliptical sectors aligned to local edges. Preserves alpha and height. High quality and large strokes cost more processing.
fx.help.bevel: Lights alpha edges or height gradients with adjustable light direction, elevation and colors. Preserves alpha and height; this is a color effect, separate from normal-map output.
fx.help.xdog: Uses an extended difference of Gaussians to extract pencil or charcoal-like detail. Optionally retains original colors. Preserves alpha and height. Scale and threshold control line coverage.
fx.help.crt: Combines barrel curvature, scanlines, RGB phosphor stripes, grain and flicker. Curvature also warps alpha and height; other controls change color. Zero rate freezes motion. Seeded frames are reproducible.
fx.help.ascii: Chooses embedded ASCII, block or binary glyphs from local luminance. Use source colors or two colors. Paper opacity only fills existing content. Glyph gaps also mask height. No system fonts are required.
fx.help.pixelSort: Actually sorts contiguous runs by luminance, hue or saturation. Thresholds and transparent cells break runs; span limits each sorted segment. Color, alpha and height move together. Analysis uses a fixed 512px short-edge grid; output samples full-resolution content. Reversed thresholds bypass sorting.
fx.pixelSortBudget: Pixel-sort analysis exceeds its budget. Increase cell size or reduce node extent.
fx.pixelSortReadback: Cannot read pixels for sorting. Reduce preview or export size and retry.
examples.creativeEffects.name: Creative effect comparison
examples.creativeEffects.description: The same heart texture shows the original and ten creative effects. Read left to right, top to bottom: original, halftone, dithering, glitch, zoom blur, painting, bevel, pencil, CRT, ASCII and pixel sorting. Select a node to inspect its settings.
examples.comicPrint.name: Comic print
examples.comicPrint.description: RGB halftones followed by edge detection, preserving the transparent heart silhouette. Reorder the effects to compare the processing order.
examples.handheld.name: Retro handheld
examples.handheld.description: Pixelation followed by four-tone handheld colors and Bayer dithering on a fixed logical pixel grid.
examples.hologramGlitch.name: Hologram glitch
examples.hologramGlitch.description: Ordered slice glitches, scanlines and bloom. Play to see interference; a fixed seed and time reproduce each frame. Random glitches do not guarantee a seamless loop.
fx.help.noiseWarp: Displaces the current composited node, sampling color, alpha and height together. Heat haze, water ripples and energy share controls in 512px short-edge units. Zero strengths or mix bypass processing. Continuous motion is not seamless; a closed loop repeats only the distortion field, so source content and other animations must also match. Uses the node boundary setting.
examples.heatHaze.name: Heat haze distortion
examples.heatHaze.description: Original on the left; the grid, ring and star on the right are composited before upward heat-haze distortion. Expand the right group to edit the source shapes. Continuous motion does not guarantee a seamless loop.
examples.waterRipples.name: Water ripple refraction
examples.waterRipples.description: Original on the left; checker tiles, ring and star on the right refract together. A three-second closed trajectory repeats the distortion over static source shapes. Edit the right group parameters or its children.
examples.energyWarp.name: Energy turbulence
examples.energyWarp.description: Original on the left; the hex grid, ring and star on the right distort together. Layered noise domain warping follows a 3.6-second closed trajectory. Edit the right group content and effect order.
fx.help.dissolve: Dissolve the current node alpha and height using noise, optionally adding charred and glowing surviving edges. Groups dissolve their composite. Progress 0 preserves the input; 1 removes it. Animate progress with keyframes; time is never accumulated.
fx.help.shockwave: Resample current content around an expanding wave ring, displacing color, alpha and height together. Progress 0 and 1 preserve the input; intermediate values propagate and fade the wave. Keyframe progress for an impact. Looping playback does not make source content seamless.
fx.help.liquidFusion: Blur the current premultiplied color, alpha and height, then reconstruct a soft silhouette. Apply to a group to join nearby children. Radius and threshold control the joining distance. Some details are lost; this is not a fluid simulation. Zero radius or mix preserves the input.
examples.burnDissolve.name: Burn dissolve comparison
examples.burnDissolve.description: Original on the left; the star and ring on the right are composited before directional burning. A three-second one-shot animates progress from 0 to 1. Edit the pattern, seed, edge color or children.
examples.shockwaveRefraction.name: Shockwave refraction comparison
examples.shockwaveRefraction.description: Original on the left; an expanding ring refracts the checker tiles, star and ring on the right. A 2.4-second one-shot displaces only the wave band. Edit the center, width, displacement and attenuation.
examples.liquidFusion.name: Liquid fusion comparison
examples.liquidFusion.description: Both sides use the same three moving circles; the right group joins them into liquid drops. The 3.2-second motion has matching endpoints. Edit the radius, threshold, uniform color or source children.
